panels.description: FreeSWITCH runtime version reported by Feature Server, together with the deployed container image tag (joined via `kube_pod_container_info` on pod). One row per (StatefulSet, FreeSWITCH version, image tag); multiple rows for the same StatefulSet indicate a rollout in progress or version drift between pods.
panels.title: FreeSWITCH Version

panels.description: Imprecise: reported by Feature Server, may not reflect actual FreeSWITCH state.
panels.title: Total Active Channels

panels.description: Percentage of FreeSWITCH media channels currently in use across the cluster: in_use / (in_use + free). Imprecise: based on Feature Server reported values, may not reflect actual FreeSWITCH state.
panels.title: Cluster Saturation
Traffic & Load Distribution (Imprecise Feature Server Metrics)

panels.description: Per-pod FreeSWITCH media CPU usage (100 - idle), as reported by the Feature Server. Static threshold lines indicate 50% (warning) and 80% (critical).
panels.title: CPU Usage %

panels.description: Direct channel count from FreeSWITCH via mod_prometheus.
panels.title: Active Channels (Native FreeSWITCH)

panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 of FreeSWITCH session (call) durations, computed from `freeswitch_session_duration_seconds_bucket` over a 5m sliding window. Sourced directly from FreeSWITCH via mod_prometheus.
panels.title: Session Duration Percentiles

panels.description: Distribution of session durations over time. Color intensity shows the number of sessions in each duration bucket.
panels.title: Session Duration Heatmap

panels.description: Should increase and decrease with call traffic. A sustained increase over days indicates a thread leak.
panels.title: Active AudioPlayer Threads

panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 time audio frames spend waiting in the queue before being processed by the AudioPlayer thread, grouped by vendor (TTS provider). High wait times indicate the player is falling behind real-time playback, which typically manifests as audio stutter or gaps.
panels.title: AudioPlayer Wait Time

panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 time spent by the AudioPlayer thread actually processing a single audio frame (after dequeue), grouped by vendor (TTS provider). High process times mean the decode/resample/write pipeline is slow; combined with elevated Wait Time this points to a saturated or under-provisioned audio pipeline.
panels.title: AudioPlayer Process Time

panels.description: p50 / p95 / p99 of the total lifetime of an AudioPlayer thread, from creation to termination, grouped by vendor (TTS provider). Reflects how long playback threads remain active per call. Abnormally long lifetimes can indicate stuck threads or a failure to release resources.
panels.title: AudioPlayer Thread Lifetime

panels.description: Live object instance counts per pod for every metric matching `*_instances` exported by the FreeSWITCH container (e.g. session, channel, endpoint, codec, and AudioPlayer instances, and any other internal object pools tracked by the VG FreeSWITCH modules). Each legend entry is `<metric_name> (<pod>)`. A steadily rising line for any metric indicates a potential memory / resource leak in that subsystem.
panels.title: Live Instance Counts

panels.description: Rate of change of instance counts (per second, smoothed over 10m). Positive values = instances accumulating. Sustained positive values indicate a leak.

targets.expr: (label_replace({__name__=~".*_instances", cluster="$cluster", container="freeswitch"}, "metric", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)") - label_replace({__name__=~".*_instances", cluster="$cluster", container="freeswitch"} offset 10m, "metric", "$1", "__name__", "(.+)")) / 600

panels.title: Instance Growth Rate (Leak Detector)

panels.description: Reader threads in mod_grpc_transcribe and mod_grpc_tts overlaid against the corresponding `_instances` gauges. Reader threads are spawned 1:1 with client instances, so the lines should track. A persistent gap → reader thread leak (positive delta) or thread spawn failure (negative delta).
panels.title: Reader Threads vs Client Instances

panels.description: Detached reaper threads still draining a closed STT WebSocket, by vendor. Self-cleaning in steady state. A sustained backlog means the upstream WS close is hanging on that vendor.
panels.title: Transcribe Reaper Threads by Vendor

panels.description: Per-second observed audio fps in the mod_grpc_transcribe media-bug callback. Target is 50 fps for L16-at-20ms. Watch for drift away from the 50 line and for the `0` / `1` rows lighting up — those are stall signals.
panels.title: Transcribe FPS Heatmap (target 50)

panels.description: Per-second observed outgoing audio fps in the mod_grpc_tts WRITE_REPLACE callback. Counted only when audio is actually written. Same 50 fps target.
panels.title: TTS FPS Heatmap (target 50)

panels.description: Share of fps observations landing in the `≤1` bucket per vendor — direct stall indicator. Rising lines mean some sessions are no longer flowing audio.
panels.title: Stall Rate (≤1 fps observations) by Vendor
gRPC Modules — Time to First Byte / First Transcript

panels.description: Latency from `start()` to the first audio chunk arriving from the upstream gRPC TTS. Captures network + auth + vendor warm-up. p95 > 2 s is a user-visible regression.
panels.title: TTS Time-to-First-Byte (p50 / p95 / p99) by Vendor

panels.description: Latency from `start()` to the first transcript event from the upstream gRPC STT. Captures connect + first interim transcript path. p95 > 1 s indicates a vendor or network problem.
panels.title: STT Time-to-First-Transcript (p50 / p95 / p99) by Vendor

panels.description: Distribution of TTS time-to-first-byte across all vendors. Look for the heat shifting up over time (worsening warm-up) or unexpected long-tail occupancy in the 5 s / 10 s buckets.
panels.title: TTS Time-to-First-Byte Heatmap

panels.description: Distribution of STT time-to-first-transcript across all vendors. Bottom row (50 ms / 100 ms) is the happy path; activity in 2.5 s / 5 s rows means some sessions are waiting much longer than expected.
panels.title: STT Time-to-First-Transcript Heatmap

panels.description: Buffer fill at the moment of consumer-side `read()` in mod_grpc_tts CircularBuffer. Steady-state should sit between the 16 KB low-watermark and 48 KB high-watermark rows. Persistent activity in the `≤4 KB` row = upstream slower than playout (starvation). Persistent activity in `64 KB` / `96 KB` rows = consumer slower than producer (backpressure / drain stall).
panels.title: TTS Buffer Bytes Heatmap (low=16 KB / high=48 KB / cap=96 KB)

panels.description: Share of buffer reads that observed ≤4 KB remaining (≤250 ms of audio left), per vendor. Sustained > 30% means the upstream gRPC TTS is delivering audio slower than playout consumes it.
panels.title: TTS Buffer Starvation Rate (≤4 KB observations) by Vendor

panels.description: STT session-start failures per minute, broken down by vendor × reason. `rpc_error` = gRPC status not OK; `server_error` = upstream returned `success=false`; `stream_open_failed` = bidi stream open failed; `reader_thread_start_failed` = std::thread ctor threw.
panels.title: STT Connect Failures by Vendor × Reason (per min)

panels.description: TTS session-start failures per minute, broken down by vendor × reason. Reason set is `stream_open_failed` and `reader_thread_start_failed`.
panels.title: TTS Connect Failures by Vendor × Reason (per min)

panels.description: Stream finished with non-OK status mid-call/playback — i.e. the upstream gRPC server hung up while we still expected to be running. Steady-state should be near zero.
panels.title: Mid-Stream Errors by Vendor (per min)

panels.description: Audio chunks the STT upstream stream rejected (`stream_->Write(chunk)` returned false). Should be ~0 in steady state. Any sustained rate is a paging-grade signal — calls are losing audio mid-flight.
panels.title: STT Audio Send Failures by Vendor (per min)
Azure TTS / Transcribe (PR #283 — 2026-05-08 NA1 freeze response)

panels.description: Per-second observed outgoing audio fps in mod_azure_tts (FrameRateObserver sampler, one tick/s per active AzureData). Target 50 fps for 20 ms PCM frames. The `0` row lighting up means TTS playout is stuck — distinct from `synthesis was never requested` because the observer only ticks while a session is active.
panels.title: Azure TTS FPS Heatmap (target 50)

panels.description: Per-second observed incoming audio fps forwarded to Azure Speech by mod_azure_transcribe. Target 50 fps. The `0` row lighting up means audio is no longer flowing to the recognizer (e.g. media-bug detached, FreeSWITCH stalled).
panels.title: Azure Transcribe FPS Heatmap (target 50)

panels.description: Azure TTS synthesis terminal outcomes split by `outcome` and `error_class`. `canceled / auth` is the 2026-05-08 fingerprint — fires on Microsoft Speech SDK CancellationErrorCode::AuthenticationFailure or Forbidden. The credential SID is intentionally not a label; identify the offending customer credential via feature-server logs.
panels.title: Azure TTS Outcomes by error_class (per min)

panels.description: Azure transcribe (STT) session terminal outcomes split by `outcome` and `error_class`. `canceled / auth` covers CancellationErrorCode::AuthenticationFailure and Forbidden — same convention as the TTS counter so one panel template covers both modules.
panels.title: Azure Transcribe Outcomes by error_class (per min)

panels.description: Number of mod_azure_tts helper threads currently blocked inside speakSsmlAsync / speakTextAsync (RAII ThreadTracker). Healthy steady-state should be near zero (single-shot synthesis completes in seconds). Sustained growth is the 2026-05-08 freeze precursor — paired alerts page at 32 (warning) and 64 (critical).
panels.title: Azure TTS Synthesis Threads In-Flight (freeze precursor)

panels.description: Rate of `canceled / auth` synthesis outcomes per pod. Alert thresholds: >0.5/s sustained 5m (warning), >2/s sustained 5m (critical — page on-call). The `for: 5m` filters brief spikes during rolling credential rotation.
panels.title: Azure TTS Auth-Failure Rate by Pod (per sec)

panels.description: STT-side mirror of the TTS auth-failure rate. Often co-fires on the same pod when a customer credential is shared between TTS and STT. Same thresholds as the TTS panel.
panels.title: Azure Transcribe Auth-Failure Rate by Pod (per sec)

panels.description: Azure TTS synthesis attempts per language (BCP-47 primary tag, malformed → `invalid`). Combined with the outcomes panel this yields the success ratio per language.
panels.title: Azure TTS Synthesis Attempts by Language (per min)

panels.description: Azure transcribe session attempts per language. Same `language` normalization as the TTS attempts counter.
panels.title: Azure Transcribe Session Attempts by Language (per min)
AudioPipe<T> WebSocket (PR #283 — STT WS terminal outcomes)

panels.description: Terminal outcomes of jambonz::AudioPipe<T> WebSocket connections — emitted from the four libwebsockets terminal callbacks (CONNECT_FAIL → error, CONNECT_SUCCESS → success, CONNECTION_CLOSED_GRACEFULLY → closed_graceful, CONNECTION_DROPPED → closed_dropped). Together with the pre-existing `jambonz_audiopipe_<provider>audiopipe_instances` gauges this distinguishes `connections cycling normally` from `connections accumulating`. Note: mod_audio_fork's non-templated drachtio::AudioPipe is NOT instrumented here.
panels.title: AudioPipe Connect Outcomes by Provider × Outcome (per min)

panels.description: Share of AudioPipe terminal outcomes that are `error` or `closed_dropped`, by provider. Alert thresholds: >10% sustained 10m (warning), >25% sustained 5m (critical — likely vendor or regional outage).
panels.title: AudioPipe Drop Rate by Provider (rolling 5m)
